articles.title_orig: Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is better than expected, but it needs some more optimization
articles.title_zh: Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is better than expected, but it needs some more optimization
articles.content_orig:
Metaphor: ReFantazio , our RPG of the Year 2024 , launches this week on Nintendo Switch 2 following the recent release of the prologue demo . Ahead of its launch, I've been playing Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 for about a week and revisiting the PS5, PS4, and Steam versions across platforms to see how the final build of the Switch 2 port looks and feels. Note that the demo only featured one graphics mode from the final game: balanced. With that in mind, Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is better than I expected, but it needs more work.
I say better because Persona 3 Reload launched in a pretty miserable state all things considered. Persona 3 Reload is also a less demanding game compared to Metaphor: ReFantazio which still has technical issues on consoles to this day. In fact, the only way to get a solid 60fps experience or smooth performance on consoles has been the PS4 version on PS5 or playing on PS5 Pro with VRR. This brings us to Nintendo Switch 2.
Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 arrives at a lower asking price than other versions, though they will all see price drops alongside the Switch 2 release. In terms of features, it has the same feature set as the console version with the addition of touchscreen support. The dash toggle present on PC that lets you dash by pressing a button instead of holding it is not present here. In that sense, Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is closer to the console versions feature wise.
Metaphor: ReFantazio's demo had no graphics options. Atlus says it uses the "balanced" mode. Metaphor: ReFantazio's demo was a confusing release with how it looked good in some ways, but lacking in others. It also had inconsistent performance. The full game offers two additional visual options, but has some of the same issues as the demo. Metaphor: ReFantazio across all three visual modes runs with an uncapped frame rate targeting 60fps. This means you could be using the prioritize "graphics" mode and have a variable experience where it can hit 60fps indoors or while looking at the ground, but it is much lower in other areas. This also applies to the menus in-game which vary in responsiveness thanks to the frame rate.
If you played the demo, which is balanced mode, you likely noticed how it felt like upscaling was only being applied to one axis with the other looking like it uses interlacing or something you'd see back in the PS3 generation. Performance mode on Switch 2 appears to have the issue in both the horizontal axis and vertical axis.
Metaphor: ReFantazio's Switch 2 performance mode runs a lot better than the graphics mode, but it doesn't hit a solid frame rate. It also looks quite awful all things considered. Given the game's aesthetic and issues on other consoles, the best way to play it on Switch 2 is the graphics mode. It has the best and most stable visuals. If this mode gets patched with an optional 30fps cap and some optimization, it will be my preferred way to play Metaphor: ReFantazio on console in general because of the issues other consoles have.
For some background, Metaphor: ReFantazio on PS5 (and PS5 Pro since it never got Pro enhancements) ran with a 1656p resolution as per Digital Foundry . When I played it on my 1440p display, it looked good, but had a lot of shimmering since there was no anti-aliasing. The PS4 Pro version, which is also how it runs on PS5 via backward compatibility, dropped the resolution to 1080p and had a lot of cuts to shadows, draw distance, and more. The PS4 and PS5 versions have no graphics modes or anything to tweak. The PC version had one ace up its sleeve, and it is a brute force solution. You could downsample from a higher resolution if your hardware was capable enough to get cleaner visuals.
On Switch 2, we have an experience that sits in between PS4 and PS5, but it has one major advantage: temporal stability. The Switch 2 has less shimmering than all other console versions during movement. The downside is the overall resolution though. Even the UI on Switch 2 renders like the PS4 version's UI. Thankfully, the Switch 2 even in its performance mode (that looks awful) has better draw distance than the PS4 version.
When it comes to performance, the only way to get a stable 60fps on console is playing the PS4 version on PS5. If you play the PS5 version on PS5 Pro, it is a mostly solid 60fps, but not perfect. There are minor drops. This is still a massively better experience than playing the PS5 version on PS5, Xbox Series version on Xbox Series X or the Switch 2 version in any of its three modes. I'm surprised Atlus didn't add a frame rate cap option, but it seems like that ship has sailed for other platforms. Since the Switch 2 port is new, I hope it gets added in updates as a 30 or 40fps (at 120hz) would be amazing on Switch 2 and make it my preferred console version.
Right now it is a bit too unstable for my liking and with how long the load times are. Metaphor on Steam Deck can deliver better visuals since you can downsample, but you aren't getting a locked 60fps experience there with good visuals. Thankfully you can cap it to 30 or 40 and get a solid portable experience. It can go much higher, but the bigger cities and final dungeon run a lot worse if you want to play at 1080p downsampled or 720p with higher settings.
To test load times, I installed Metaphor: ReFantazio on the Switch 2 internal storage, the PS5 version on PS5 internal storage and PS4 Pro internal storage, the PS4 version on PS5 internal storage, and the Steam version on the Steam Deck OLED internal storage. I measured the time taken to get to the title screen from the dashboard, loading a save, and area transition time. I tested area transition time because it felt too long in the Switch 2 demo. The results below are in seconds and I mashed confirm to speed up the loading and skip any cut-scenes.
As you can see, the Switch 2 has the fastest initial load, but is the slowest when in-game. The PS5 version on PS5 Pro is the bestest in-game followed by the PS5 version. I hope the area transition and other load times when in-game on Switch 2 can be improved in updates.
Aside from no frame rate caps which I hope get added as options, Metaphor: ReFantazio's load times are a bit too long when in-game. Beyond this, I would like to see the UI support higher resolutions and at least have the menus run at 60fps if the gameplay itself is lower. The variable performance affecting menus and responsiveness is annoying.
In its current state, Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is a lot better than I expected, but more work needs to be done. The visual options are good to have, but it looks quite rough in its performance mode. It also doesn't help that despite the downgrades to visuals in that mode, it can't hit a stable frame rate. I recommend playing with the quality mode enabled and tolerating the inconsistent performance for the best possible experience on Switch 2 right now. I do appreciate that the overall image is more temporally stable than other consoles at least. Hopefully Atlus continues to optimize and update this because performance caveats aside, Metaphor: ReFantazio is solid enough all things considered.

articles.title_orig: Apple’s new HomeView to add two major features not yet announced, per leaks
articles.title_zh: Apple’s new HomeView to add two major features not yet announced, per leaks
articles.content_orig:
Apple’s HomeView arrives this Friday ( pre-order here ), but leaks indicate there are already two major new features in the works that haven’t been announced. Here’s what to expect.
It’s been a busy product launch season for Apple, and the company isn’t done quite yet.
Two new Home products arrive in stores this Friday, November 13: Apple HomeView and the new Apple TV 4K .
Yet despite the HomeView still being days away from launch, leaks in Apple code have already revealed two unannounced features that are in the works.
Leaker pdfu discovered evidence in HomeView 27.2 software that Apple is preparing for the product to add security camera functionality.
Apple HomeView could soon double as a HomeKit security camera. The feature has concrete settings localization in HomeView Software 27.2, describing functionality and privacy protections. Here are the exact localization strings: Setup Page Your HomeView can be used as a… pic.twitter.com/NsnknajWKd
Based on pdfu’s findings, much of the work has already been done for HomeView to integrate with HomeKit Secure Video.
However, Apple hasn’t announced any sort of security camera functionality, so there’s clearly still more work to be done and it’s always possible the feature is never enabled.
Additionally, pdfu found a key change in iOS 27.3’s beta that reveals support for third-party AI apps is coming to HomeView.
HomeView has a unique third-party app story. There’s no App Store, but the product can run CarPlay-compatible apps from your iPhone automatically. At launch, only audio and video apps will be supported.
But iOS 27.3’s beta code adds “conversational apps” as a third category of supported apps. That’s what AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude are classified as in CarPlay.
Nobody should buy a HomeView in the hope of these two features being added. But if you are interested in HomeView, it sounds like Apple has an ambitious set of software updates planned for its new product.
You can pre-order Apple’s HomeView here for $299 .
Would either of these HomeView additions impact a purchase decision for you? Let us know in the comments.

For two years he co-hosted the Adapt podcast on Relay FM, which focused entirely on the iPad. As a result, it should come as no surprise that his favorite Apple device is the iPad Pro.

articles.title_orig: GTA VI will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming for Xbox One consoles
articles.title_zh: GTA VI will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming for Xbox One consoles
articles.content_orig:
Rockstar Games confirms GTA VI will run at 30fps across all consoles.
Rockstar Games confirms GTA VI will run at 30fps across all consoles.
Rockstar Games is making Grand Theft Auto VI available on Xbox Cloud Gaming when it launches next week. While you’d normally assume that would mean Grand Theft Auto VI would be available to stream on phones, PCs, the web, Xbox consoles, and even TVs, it appears to be restricted to just Xbox Series X / S and Xbox One consoles.
That does mean that anyone with an older Xbox One console can stream Grand Theft Auto VI instead of having to upgrade to a PS5 or Xbox Series S / X console to play. Rockstar notes that Xbox Cloud Gaming will use the Xbox Series S graphics settings to stream to Xbox consoles.
Xbox’s own announcement blog post only mentions Xbox Cloud Gaming streaming for Xbox Series X / S and Xbox One owners. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma says the cloud deal for Grand Theft Auto VI is “the first step in our new 10-year strategic partnership with Take-Two.” Sharma also says the game is “the most pre-ordered game ever on Microsoft Store.” Microsoft is also planning to add Grand Theft Auto V , Red Dead Redemption 2 , and more to Xbox Cloud Gaming in “the coming months.”
What this all means is that Microsoft effectively has an exclusive on streaming Grand Theft Auto VI from the cloud for launch, albeit only to Xbox consoles.
I originally reported last month that Microsoft had secured exclusive Grand Theft Auto VI cloud streaming rights, but Xbox chief strategy officer Matthew Ball revealed on X that Microsoft wouldn’t be streaming Grand Theft Auto VI exclusively. While Microsoft’s contract might not specifically state exclusive, the end result is exclusive cloud gaming on Xbox, for now. Sony may well eventually announce its own cloud streaming plans for the game, but Rockstar Games notes that Grand Theft Auto VI “will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.” That’s not cloud streaming, though.
I also initially reported that Grand Theft Auto VI would be available to stream on PC, simply because the entire point of Xbox Cloud Gaming is to make games available on Xbox consoles, TVs, PCs, and the web. It’s strange to see a rare exception for Grand Theft Auto VI , but not entirely surprising. Perhaps Microsoft will eventually be able to stream the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI whenever it launches.
Rockstar Games also confirms Grand Theft Auto VI will run at 30fps across PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series S / X consoles. The main advantage of a PS5 Pro is ray-traced shadows and support for PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR).

articles.title_orig: EU budget battle erupts as four countries defy Merz over Ukraine aid
articles.title_zh: EU budget battle erupts as four countries defy Merz over Ukraine aid
articles.content_orig:
The leaders of Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Bulgaria have pushed back against German Chancellor Friedrich Merz's ultimatum to make approval of the EU's next long-term budget conditional on fresh financial support for Ukraine.
Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico denounced the move as a "textbook case of blackmail" and threatened to wield his veto.
"We have an equal say in this matter," Fico said on Tuesday as he welcomed his Czech counterpart, Andrej Babiš, in Bratislava.
"Just as Mr Merz talks about using his veto, I can say exactly the same. We have the same veto power as the German federal chancellor."
Babiš quipped that Merz "probably doesn't realise" that the proposed EU budget already earmarks €100 billion for Ukraine. However, those funds will not become available until 2028, while Kyiv faces a €70 billion shortfall next year.
"Today will not be business as usual – not by a long shot. Today, we must respond to blackmail," Fico said, expressing his displeasure.
"What the federal chancellor is doing is a textbook case of blackmail, and I reject it. We are a sovereign country. We are the Slovak Republic. We have our own views."
Merz upped the ante in a letter to European Council President António Costa, declaring that fresh aid for Ukraine was an "essential prerequisite" for approving the next EU budget. The move effectively links two highly contentious issues, both of which require unanimity.
Brussels has promised to cover two-thirds of Ukraine's €70 billion gap, roughly €45 billion, through a yet-to-be-defined instrument. Given the massive scale of the needs, a new round of joint debt has quickly emerged as the frontrunner option.
The new funding would come on top of an existing €90 billion support loan, from which Slovakia, the Czech Republic and Hungary secured exemptions.
"Supporting Ukraine is a matter of our indivisible European security, and so must be the burden sharing for that support," Merz wrote.
Merz received Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar in Berlin on Tuesday, just a day after the letter became public.
At the end of the bilateral meeting, Magyar made clear he opposed linking the EU budget with Ukraine aid, arguing the two issues are intrinsically distinct .
"It is possible, obviously, that it has to do a lot with politics. I do not consider this to be blackmail. So I do not use any such words, because everything is connected to everything in today's world," he said, referring to Fico's earlier comments.
"But I think that this does not necessarily have a good message."
Magyar said Hungary could not commit to fresh debt at the European level because it is already struggling to rein in its soaring public deficit.
"In this regard, this is obviously unacceptable for us for domestic political reasons, but we will negotiate in Berlin, Dublin and Brussels," he said.
"We will find a solution for the EU budget. I am sure of it."
Speaking in Varna, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev also pointed to high deficit levels as a reason to exempt his country from future credit lines to Ukraine. Radev said his country will continue support through other means, such as energy flows.
"Bulgaria is in no way blocking the decisions at the Council level that are taken in unity for everyone to support (Ukraine) as they can," Radev said.
Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Bulgaria all belong to the "Friends of Cohesion", a group of 17 countries that wants to protect cohesion and agricultural funds in the next long-term EU budget. This has put them on a collision course with the "frugals", who demand across-the-board reductions.
The "frugals" include some of the largest donors to Ukraine, such as Germany, and resent how Slovakia, the Czech Republic, Hungary and Bulgaria are trying to opt out of support to Ukraine while, at the same time, demanding cohesion funds.
Speaking alongside Magyar in Berlin, Merz insisted that support for Ukraine must be shared more fairly.
"It's not a good option to continue down this path. Ukraine policy should be fully included in the European Union budget," he said.
"At least four countries think differently, but it is definitely important to talk about this."

articles.content_orig:
Fresh details about the Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 successor suggest that the upcoming model will be offered exclusively as a coupe.
Unlike the more powerful Dark Horse SC, which is available with both a fixed roof and a soft-top convertible, the new variant will not get an open-top version. This also follows the approach taken with the previous S550-generation Shelby GT350, which was sold only as a coupe.
Pricing is expected to position the car between the standard Dark Horse and the Dark Horse SC. The 2026 Dark Horse starts at around $65,000, while the SC carries a much higher starting price of approx $106,000. A price in the $80,000 range could make sense for the new model, although Ford has yet to confirm anything.
Its official name remains under wraps, but the Dark Horse badge is expected to feature somewhere in it. The new Mustang is reportedly scheduled to reach dealerships in 2027 as a 2027 model-year offering.

articles.title_orig: Number of arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.title_zh: Number of arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.content_orig:
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.
In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.
It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.
Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.
It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".
The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.
The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.
The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson.
The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims:
"At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities.
"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.
"Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations.
"The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office."
A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation.
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.
One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.
Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.
Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.
In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.
"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.
"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."
The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."
The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line .

articles.title_orig: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
articles.title_zh: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
articles.content_orig:
FILE - In this photo provided by the North Korean government, its leader Kim Jong Un, center, and his daughter, reportedly named Kim Ju Ae, visit a military training base in North Korea, Thursday, March 19, 2026. Independent journalists were not given access to cover the event depicted in this image distributed by the North Korean government. The content of this image is as provided and cannot be independently verified. 朝鮮通信社/KCNA via KNS via AP hide caption
SEOUL, South Korea — Until she fled North Korea three years ago, Kim Yumi felt deeply frustrated whenever state TV showed leader Kim Jong Un with his young daughter. The message, she felt, was clear and worrying: North Korea was laying the groundwork for an eventual hereditary transfer of power, this time to Kim's daughter.
Publicly questioning the Kim dynasty's hold on power would mean severe persecution. Already angered by draconian pandemic regulations that ruined her family's fishing business, she defected to South Korea by boat with her family.
"My husband and I didn't want our children to live under a fourth-generation dictatorship. As parents, we thought the best thing we could do for our children was to give them freedom," said Kim Yumi, 32, who now lives in Seoul.
North Korea allows no dissent and harshly punishes attempts to flee the country. Established in 1948, the nation is nominally a socialist republic, but in reality it is an authoritarian dynasty, with three generations of the Kim family ruling in succession. There was no known public resistance during its previous two successions — from state founder Kim Il Sung to his son Kim Jong Il in 1994 and then from Kim Jong Il to his son Kim Jong Un in 2011.
This time, North Korea is apparently trying something radical.
Kim Jong Un's repeated public appearances with his daughter over the past four years have led to speculation that she's being groomed as her father's heir.
The question of who will become North Korea's next leader is crucial because that person will face a huge challenge — governing an impoverished, nuclear-armed nation whose 26 million people have little political freedom and live under strict state surveillance while being cut off from much of the outside world.
North Koreans have no say in the selection of their future leader, and analysts and defectors say they will passively accept a third dynastic succession — at least publicly.
To gauge North Koreans' private views, The Associated Press spoke with nearly a dozen defectors who still have contacts in North Korea or witnessed the country's previous power successions, as well as several experts.
Not much is known about Kim's daughter except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae.
Since late 2022, she has made dozens of public appearances, all of them with her father at big events like weapons tests and military parades. State media has called her Kim's "most beloved" and "respected" child. Her status has been emphasized by images showing an elderly general kneeling before her and her standing in front of her father.
South Korea's spy agency says she is Kim's likely heir. Eight of the 11 defectors interviewed by the AP shared that view; the others disagreed, citing the North's deeply patriarchal culture.
"During her visits to missile launch sites and factories, the way senior North Korean officials treat Kim Ju Ae involves protocols reserved for a successor, not the ones simply for a daughter of Kim Jong Un," said Tae Yongho, a former minister at North Korea's Embassy in London who defected to South Korea in 2016. "They are repeating the same protocol and treatment they provided for Kim Jong Un," when he accompanied his father as his heir.
Tae Yongho, a former minister of North Korea's Embassy in London who defected to South Korea in 2016, speaks during an interview with The Associated Press in Seoul, South Korea, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. Lee Jin-man/AP hide caption
Kang Mi-Jin, a defector who runs a company analyzing North Korea's economy, said her contacts inside the North told her over smuggled phones that they think Kim Ju Ae is in line to succeed her father.
Jung Gwang-il, a defector who specializes in smuggling outside information to North Korea, said the North Koreans he meets as they visit Chinese border towns also hold the same belief.
Former NBA star Dennis Rodman was the first to reveal her identity, holding her as a baby during a 2013 trip to Pyongyang.
Much of the skepticism about Kim Ju Ae as a potential leader stems from her being female. South Korean officials believe she has a younger sibling whose gender hasn't been confirmed.
Women in North Korea remain deeply underrepresented in senior posts. Only one of 17 department directors for the ruling Workers' Party is a woman. That woman is Kim Jong Un's influential younger sister, Kim Yo Jong, according to South Korea's Unification Ministry.
"My contacts in North Korea say it would be nonsensical to revere that little girl as their supreme leader," said Kim Jeong-Ah, a former North Korean army officer who resettled in South Korea in 2009.
Lee Si-young, a defector who heads the Seoul-based Free North Korea Radio station, said that some of her older contacts in North Korea aren't happy with a woman taking power. But she said members of the Kim family "are like gods reigning over humans so gender really doesn't matter."
Whether or not the girl succeeds her father, observers agree that Kim Jong Un, 42, is likely to designate one of his children to prolong his family's rule, a move they expect would face little resistance at home. South Korea's spy agency recently assessed that Kim is extremely obese and at high risk of cardiovascular disease but shows no other signs of poor health.
North Koreans will passively "accept a hereditary succession as something that they should go along with," said Ahn Chan-il, a defector and scholar who heads the World Institute for North Korean Studies in Seoul.
During North Korea's first leadership transition, in 1994, the new leader, Kim Jong Il, then 52, had already spent two decades as the official successor working alongside his father to run the country.
The second succession, in 2011, was more uncertain. Kim Jong Un, who was then 27, was seen by outsiders as too young and inexperienced. He quickly consolidated his grip on power, however, by orchestrating high-profile executions and purges, including the 2013 killing of his powerful uncle Jang Song Thaek.
"A hereditary power succession system has been institutionalized in North Korea, just like presidential elections in our system," said Oh Gyeong-seob, an analyst at Seoul's Korea Institute for National Unification. "North Korea's ruling elite accepts it as a matter of course. So do its general citizens."
Choi Song-juk, who fled North Korea in 2015, said she had been so brainwashed that she had no complaints about the North's two earlier power successions. She now calls them "nonsense."
Defector Jeon Jae-hyun said North Korea's pervasive surveillance apparatus keeps people from voicing their discontent with the government and helps enforce political loyalty.
Defector Kim Yumi said she had never heard about the girl until Kim Jong Un publicly introduced his daughter at a long-range missile launch site in November 2022.
"Ordinary people know absolutely nothing about private lives of the Kim family," said Kim Yumi, who now runs a YouTube channel on North Korea. "They don't really try to know about it and don't pay attention to it because doing so could put them in danger."

articles.title_orig: Netanyahu Calls Trump "Every Day" To Push Him To Renew Iran Strikes: Report
articles.title_zh: Netanyahu Calls Trump "Every Day" To Push Him To Renew Iran Strikes: Report
articles.content_orig:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Monday that the war with Iran could end "fairly soon," adding that Tehran was "talking very politely" with Washington.
Trump told reporters in the White House Monday, after a meeting with Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, that "We're seeing momentum toward the end of this conflict. I think it's going to be ending fairly soon."
"Iran militarily is effectively over," Trump said, citing the destruction of its navy and surging inflation that he said has hollowed out its economy.
Qatar, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait would "prefer the status quo" which involves maintaining the naval blockade against Iran and "Operation Iron Gate" — a task force announced on Saturday aimed at preventing Iran from using ground routes to transport advanced weapons and other materials — Trump said in a Truth Social post.
He reiterated that Iran would not be allowed to have a nuclear weapon and kept the door open for potentially resuming strikes should circumstances change. "America is 'docked and loaded' and ready to go," he said, though caveating that new strikes were "quite unlikely."
The conflict, now in its ninth month, has driven a surge in fuel prices, hitting nearly every sector of the global economy.
The U.S. had reportedly planned for a potential increase in naval forces in the Middle East in the run-up to the midterm elections, with Trump hinting at escalating the conflict after the results.
The administration has since toned down the war rhetoric after bruising midterm election results that saw Republicans lose both chambers of Congress as voters expressed frustration with soaring living costs stemming from the war.
A diplomat briefed on the Qatar meeting told Axios that Trump told Al Thani that he wanted a deal and would give talks a chance, but could reverse course if Iran does not take the negotiations seriously.
Iran has put forward a two-day proposal to the U.S. via Qatari mediators, Reuters reported, citing a senior Iranian official , demanding lifting of the sanctions imposed on Tehran and a new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. Washington was reviewing the proposal, according to the report.
Iranian officials have disputed that talks with Washington were underway. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, reportedly said that Washington should stop "manufacturing fake news about imaginary talks."
Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday on the prospect of de-escalation, extending losses from the previous day. U.S. West Texas Intermediate dropped over 1% to $85.8 per barrel, after sliding more than 4% in the prior session. Brent futures dropped more than 1% to $91.56 a barrel, hovering near 10-week low levels.

articles.title_orig: Adobe brings AI agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly
articles.title_zh: Adobe brings AI agents and new creative tools to Photoshop, Premiere, and Firefly
articles.content_orig:
Adobe is pouring more AI into its products, including Photoshop, Premiere, Illustrator, and InDesign, in a major product feature announcement at its MAX event in Miami. The company is also expanding AI capabilities in its creative tool, Firefly, and releasing a Model Context Protocol (MCP) that lets other chatbots like ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini use Adobe features.
Adobe’s Firefly app is moving into Figma’s territory with a new prototyping tool in private beta called Builder, which lets users create designs to show off ideas. There is also a new tool to create on-brand graphs, along with an image-editing tool that lets you change part of an image without changing other objects.
A new AI-powered video tool in Firefly will allow users to assemble a video from clips and other elements like images and sound effects. The company is making its agent proactive and always on so that it can get more context about work and be present for any action. Adobe is also making it easier for people to take quick action, like removing the background or generating a thumbnail for a video.
The company has already added a ton of AI features across its apps like Photoshop, Express, Premiere, and Illustrator . At the MAX event, Adobe is continuing the trend. Photoshop is getting a new relighting feature and sliders for prompt-based generative styles; Premiere will have a new color grading system for professionals and an object removal feature for video; and Lightroom has a way to correct blinking eyes and a blemish removal tool.
Adobe already offers a lot of third-party models from companies like Google, Runway, ElevenLabs, Black Forest Labs, OpenAI, Kling, and ByteDance. One of its newer acquisitions, Topaz Labs , is releasing two image models, called Wonder 4 for upscaling and denoising, and ImageHDR, to turn standard images into HDR.
The company already has ChatGPT and Claude integrations to let users access some of its product functions. Now, Adobe is releasing a local MCP to expose more features of its Creative Cloud apps to users.
Adobe vice president Deepa Subramaniam told TechCrunch that the company is still figuring out what capabilities to expose and will rely on user feedback.
“We are still figuring out where and when and how to draw the line. What we’re putting out there is a number of endpoints and capabilities across Illustrator, Photoshop, After Effects, and Premiere. We’re just going to see how people use it, what they’re trying to do, and keep showing more. We don’t have any need or desire to sort of limit what the MCP endpoint can expose. What we really want to do is to support that creative workflow, how you choose to do it,” said Subramaniam.
Last month, Adobe rival Figma co-founder Dylan Field said at an event in India that MCP is not a perfect standard and benefits frontier labs more .

articles.title_orig: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
articles.title_zh: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
articles.content_orig:
Sign up now: Get insights on Asia's fast-moving developments
Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka at the annual State of the Nation Address in Jakarta on Aug 14. Indonesian MPs are gearing up to launch a motion of opinion against him, part of a step towards a possible impeachment.
Published Nov 10, 2026, 05:45 PM
Updated Nov 10, 2026, 09:40 PM
JAKARTA – Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka told President Prabowo Subianto on Nov 10 that he intends to resign from his post amid mounting efforts to impeach him.
State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said that Gibran has also asked for a chance to prove in court the validity of his education documents – that he had completed senior high school which is a prerequisite under election laws to hold office – following a 2½ -hour meeting between Gibran and Prabowo in the morning.
Local media reported the meeting took place at the President’s official residence in the Widya Chandra complex in Jakarta.
Gibran “expressed his intention to resign in the face of developments relating to the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court decisions”, Prasetyo told reporters.
He said Gibran also asked to be given the opportunity via the State Administrative Court process to prove his educations documents are valid.
Gibran told reporters afterwards at the presidential palace that he views Prabowo “as a father” and appreciates the latter’s advice.
“President Prabowo is like a father to me. He has given me a lot of advice and input on the current developments,” Gibran said.
“One piece of his advice is that I keep fighting in the State Administrative Court... and file a civil review appeal to the Supreme Court’s ruling.”
On Oct 6, the Constitutional Court dismissed a petition over Gibran’s eligibility but said in its reasoning that it found no document showing he had completed overseas education equivalent to senior high school.
Later, a Supreme Court ruling on Oct 30 invalidated the high-school equivalency certificate Gibran used to register as a vice-presidential candidate in 2024.
This comes as Indonesian MPs are gearing up to launch a motion of opinion against Gibran, part of a step towards a possible impeachment. Parliament resumed hearings on Nov 10 after a month-long recess. The Straits Times understands that forms to launch the motion have been circulating among MPs for signature since Nov 7.
It also comes amid a widely reported strain between Prabowo and his predecessor Joko Widodo, Gibran’s father.
Under the so-called MD3 Law, a motion of opinion needs the signatures of at least 25 of the 580 MPs, about 4.3%, from more than one of Parliament’s eight factions.
It must then be approved in a plenary session attended by at least two-thirds of MPs, with at least two-thirds of those present voting in favour. That means 387 votes if all 580 MPs attend, or 258 if only the 387 needed for a quorum do. If passed, the case goes to the Constitutional Court.
If the court finds there has been a serious breach of law or Gibran is no longer eligible to serve as vice-president, the People’s Consultative Assembly makes the final decision. Any decision that Gibran is no longer eligible will require a three-quarter quorum and two-thirds approval.
The MD3 Law governs the People’s Consultative Assembly, the House of Representatives, the Regional Representatives Council and regional legislatures. It sets out their powers and procedures, including the House’s rights to question the government (interpellation), investigate it (inquiry), and state a formal opinion.
Protesters sitting near a banner during a protest calling for the impeachment of Indonesian Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka outside the Parliament building in Jakarta on Nov 10.
Since the Constitutional Court ruling on Oct 6, there have been scattered protests across Indonesia demanding Gibran’s resignation or impeachment.
On Nov 10, several small groups of protesters rallied in front of the Parliament building in Central Jakarta demanding that lawmakers start the impeachment process.
Banners hung outside the Parliament gates bore slogans like “#GibranOut” and “Impeach Gibran”.
Meri Samiri, coordinator of a group of around a dozen women calling themselves the National Coalition of Indonesian Women, said that they had been protesting outside the building for 21 days.
“We have been collecting signatures from many people who agree that Gibran should resign or be dismissed, including from Jimly Asshiddiqie,” she told reporters, referring to a former chief justice of the Supreme Court.
She said that the coalition wanted Gibran to resign because they felt that the Indonesian people deserved to be led by “someone who has integrity and competence”.
“We want a leader who has a real diploma,” she said.
Wahyudi Soeriaatmadja has been Indonesia correspondent at The Straits Times since 2008, and is based in Jakarta.
Karina Tehusijarana is Indonesia Correspondent for The Straits Times.

articles.title_orig: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
articles.title_zh: Iran rejects French claims it was behind supermarket fridge hacking
articles.content_orig:
Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile".
On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression".
He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions.
The French cyber-attacks, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food, were followed by a similar hacks against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.
Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".
He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".
France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.
The Paris prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.
Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.
Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.
In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.
On Monday, some Iranian media outlets denied the French accusations, but there had been no official comment until Tuesday's statement from Iran's foreign ministry.
On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.
More than 100 of Coopérative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from Intermarché and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.
Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.
In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.
The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.
Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian.

articles.title_orig: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
articles.title_zh: French wartime resistance heroine Solange Alexandre dies aged 104
articles.content_orig:
Solange Alexandre twice turned down the LÃ©gion d'Honneur before relenting in 2024
One of France's last Resistance heroes from World War Two has died at the age of 104.  Solange Alexandre was also a rare woman who, with her future husband, created and commanded her own unit of anti-German fighters.
After serving as a Resistance courier from 1941, three years later she founded the Pas-de-Boeuf network near the town of RuillÃ©-sur-Loir.
With some 30 men under her orders, she organised sabotage operations, sheltered Allied airmen and, after the Allied landings in Normandy on D-Day in 1944, joined the fight against the occupying German forces.
President Emmanuel Macron was among many to pay tribute to Alexandre, after her death was announced at a nursing home in Le Mans.
"She said she only ever did her duty. But her duty was our freedom. France will never forget. Thank you," Macron posted on social media.
Born in 1922 in the Sarthe department of western France,  Solange Alexandre, nÃ©e Dubuisson, grew up in a patriotic family that had suffered in World War One.
"My mother lost her first husband in the war, and my father was wounded in 1917.   The words homeland and honour were very important to us. They were in my blood," she recalled in her memoirs.
In June 1940 she heard on the radio the appeal from General Charles de Gaulle in London, calling on the French not to give up the struggle against Germany.  She had never heard of him, but that did not matter.
"From that moment I knew I had to join up," she wrote.
Some months later she was recruited by a friend of her father's â a Tunisian-born French army veteran called SaÃ¯d Belhaffaf, who had joined the Resistance.
Using the code-name Corlay, she criss-crossed the region around Le Mans by bicycle, gathering information and passing on messages.
"There were no mobile phones back then, and no private cars either because of the lack of petrol. The bicycle was king," she said in an interview two years ago.
In 1943 she met her first husband Guy DÃ©liot, who had deserted from the French gendarmerie after refusing to arrest some Jews.
The following April, with the Allied invasion approaching, they decided to take to the maquis, in other words live clandestinely in the forested hills, supplied with food by local farmers.
Their group consisted of deserters from German forced labour programmes, as well as survivors from another Resistance outfit that had been destroyed by the enemy.  There were also two airmen, one American and one Canadian.
"Twice the Gestapo came for me, and twice I slipped through their hands," she later recalled.
After taking part in the liberation of Tours in September 1944, she ended the war with the rank of sub-lieutenant in the French Interior Forces (FFI).
Later she worked as a teacher and followed her husband on his many postings as an officer of the gendarmerie in French overseas territories. He was killed in 1960 in Martinique, and in 1981 she remarried.
Twice Solange Alexandre turned down the LÃ©gion d'Honneur , saying that she had only done her duty and that others were more worthy.
Finally in 2024 she relented.
On receiving the award she said: "It is a great pleasure and a great honour.  I am very proud â even if it is only a few weeks, or a few months, before I die."

articles.title_orig: Europe and US agree to review postwar continental security as Ukraine talks begin
articles.title_zh: Europe and US agree to review postwar continental security as Ukraine talks begin
articles.content_orig:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here .
ABU DHABI, United Arab Emirates — Three-way talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States opened Tuesday in the United Arab Emirates as Washington made another push to end the war that followed Moscow’s all-out invasion of its neighbor nearly five years ago.
Hopes of ending Europe’s biggest conflict since World War II are tempered by the absence of any significant breakthroughs in three previous rounds of talks earlier this year.
There’s nothing to suggest a new posture that would lead to a breakthrough, but circumstances surrounding the talks have been changed by the outcome of the U.S. midterm elections as well as increased pressure on Russia’s wartime economy. Moscow also is seeking to break Ukrainians’ will as winter sets in by ramping up its battering of the country’s power grid.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the nearly four-hour talks were “constructive and quite substantive,” and largely were about humanitarian issues, including prisoner exchanges and returning Ukrainian civilians in captivity, as well as children taken from the country. Security guarantees also were discussed, he added during an appearance at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark.
Speaking in Paris at the Group of Seven meeting, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the talks were “very productive,” but added: “There’s a lot of work to be done in that regard.”
The two-day session in the UAE’s capital, Abu Dhabi, is the first such meeting since February on the war, which analysts and humanitarian organizations say has killed hundreds of thousands of soldiers and thousands of civilians. A second round is expected Wednesday.
President Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, who along with U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff is trying to broker a settlement, said he believed there were “some good ideas how to bridge” the differences between the two sides.
Trump, whose stance on the war has varied, must reckon with Democrats taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. elections. Democrats could demand more support for Ukraine.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz told ZDF television on Monday night that “I don’t have overly high expectations” for the talks.
There are no signs the fighting is abating, and the talks come against a backdrop of new long-range strikes by both Russia and Ukraine. The two armies are largely deadlocked on the front line.
Russia launched 162 drones of various types and a ballistic missile at Ukraine overnight, Ukraine’s air force said.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces downed 155 Ukrainian drones overnight in eight Russian regions, as well as over the Crimean Peninsula, which Moscow illegally annexed from Ukraine in 2014.
Kushner said in opening remarks that the goal of the talks is to “create a new framework and a new understanding building upon the different institutions and understandings of the past.”
“We take what’s worked, we try to identify what’s failed, why we’re in this position and hopefully create a new framework that leads us for decades, if not centuries, of peace,” he said.
NATO commander U.S. Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, who was also present, pointed to “some great progress in the past in a military-to-military dialogue in a trilateral format.”
He said that the U.S. delegation looked forward “to working with both sides as we seek to advance the progress we’ve made in the past and continue this pursuit to set the foundations for a lasting peace.”
Rustem Umerov, the head of Ukraine’s Foreign Intelligence Service who leads Kyiv’s delegation, thanked the U.S. for its efforts to end Russia’s invasion.
“Our people are waiting to end this war. And we hope that we will achieve the lasting peace for Ukraine,” he said.
The head of the Russian delegation, Vladimir Medinsky, expressed hope the meeting “will allow us to advance on the path towards peace in the interests of the people of Russia and the people of Ukraine.”
Umerov said the day began with a meeting between the Ukrainian team, the U.S. envoys and representatives from the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, NATO and the European Commission.
The Russian and Ukrainian governments remain far apart on key elements of any prospective deal.
Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to pull its troops back from four regions of Ukraine that Moscow annexed in September 2022 but has never fully captured. He also demands that Ukraine abandon its bid to join NATO, accept strict limits on its military and drop restrictions on the Russian language and the Moscow-affiliated Orthodox Church in Ukraine.
Putin wants a comprehensive peace deal on those conditions and won’t agree to a general halt in hostilities, arguing that it would only allow Ukrainian troops to rest and replenish their weapons stockpiles.
Zelensky rejects Putin’s demands to voluntarily cede territory. He also rejects any limits on Ukraine’s military or its arrangements with Western partners, which Kyiv sees as essential security guarantees to stop Moscow from invading again.
Ukraine argues an immediate ceasefire is the necessary first step toward negotiating a wider settlement and says a direct meeting between Putin and Zelensky is the only way territorial issues can be settled. Putin has spurned those suggestions.
The Russian and Ukrainian delegations include senior officials who have attended previous rounds of talks.
Russia’s chief negotiator is Medinsky, a Putin aide who has led Moscow’s team since the first direct peace talks with Ukraine in Istanbul in March 2022. The Russian delegation also includes deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and deputy chief of the General Staff’s operational department Yuri Zhigarlovsky.
Besides Umerov, the Ukrainian delegation also reportedly includes Zelensky’s chief of staff, Kyrylo Budanov, his deputy, Sergiy Kyslytsya, and Davyd Arakhamia, the parliamentary faction leader of Zelensky’s Servant of the People party.
Last week, Trump declared that some kind of grand deal about European security was in the works, describing it as “a big agreement” that is “going to involve more than Ukraine.”
Kushner said Monday on X that a “comprehensive and lasting settlement will also require direct engagement between Russia and our European partners on the broader security arrangements that affect them.”
Moscow has praised the broad approach.
“We can only welcome the (U.S.) negotiators on President Donald Trump’s request proposing to put the issue of collective security on top of the agenda of the talks on a Ukrainian settlement,” Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said.
Some in the European Union see Washington’s proposals as too accommodating to Moscow.
Russia has objected to the Europeans’ involvement in the three-way talks, but said EU representatives could join at a later stage.
Hatoum writes for the Associated Press.

articles.title_zh: I Visited China as an American Without a Visa—Here’s How You Can Do It Too
articles.content_orig:
By JO MACFARLANE, HEALTH REPORTER
Published: 02:01 EST, 18 October 2026 | Updated: 05:58 EST, 26 October 2026
Sitting in the park with her grandchildren one afternoon, Becky Tucker decided to overhaul her life.
As the four of them played and ran around, Becky, then 48, simply lacked the energy to join in. It was, she says now, a wake-up call.
The risk management consultant from Poole, Dorset, had been struggling with fatigue, anxiety, mood swings and hot flushes as perimenopause took hold.
And for as long as she could remember, she had experienced intense, debilitating migraines for a week every month, linked to her menstrual cycle.
She was also significantly overweight – something she had struggled with her whole life. At more than 13 stone and with a BMI of 29 – bordering on obese – Becky had spent the previous 25 years on various weight-loss plans.
They'd worked, to begin with, but then she piled on the pounds again when she returned to her usual diet of chocolate bars and what she calls 'beige stodge'.
It will be a familiar scenario to many in midlife – the pounds creep on until it no longer feels possible to shift them.
But three years on, it is no exaggeration to say that Becky is transformed. Indeed, as our photos show so clearly, she is almost unrecognisable. Fizzing with energy and an astonishing four stone lighter, she says she feels like a different woman.
Becky Tucker shed four stone by following the ZOE diet. The risk management consultant from Poole, Dorset, had  previously struggled with fatigue, anxiety, mood swings and hot flushes
At more than 13 stone and with a BMI of 29 – bordering on obese – Becky had spent the previous 25 years on various weight-loss plans
Previous diets worked, but then she'd pile on the pounds again when she returned to her usual routine of chocolate bars and 'beige stodge'
Her enviably slender figure has shrunk by more than four dress sizes, from a 16 to an 8 or 10. Her near-lifelong migraines have vanished, as have those limiting menopause symptoms.
And most importantly of all? She is now running around the park with her grandchildren, no longer stuck on a bench at the sidelines.
But what is extraordinary is that Becky achieved it – and she says this almost apologetically – 'without really trying'.
There was no restrictive diet, no calorie counting, and no pangs of hunger. Instead, Becky overhauled her diet with the help of gut health science company ZOE, co-founded by Professor Tim Spector, the scientist at the forefront of discoveries in diet and gut health and their impact on our overall health – and, research increasingly suggests, our mood.
Hi, I'm Professor Tim Spector, a medical scientist at King's College London, co-founder of ZOE and author of Good Mood Food.
I've spent decades researching how the food we eat affects our weight, mood and brain health. Now I'd like to share what I've discovered with you.
My exclusive six-week ZOE diet plan will show you how to eat your way to better health, with delicious recipes, simple changes and no calorie counting.
You could even lose up to a stone in time for the Christmas party season. And for DailyMail+ subscribers, it's completely free.
Click here to sign up and start your six-week ZOE diet
Research by Professor Spector, an honorary consulting physician and expert in epidemiology at King's College London, suggests that simple changes to our food choices can have remarkable benefits – from helping us lose weight without going hungry to improving our mood, boosting energy and potentially protecting our brains against the effects of ageing.
And now, in an exclusive new six-week newsletter series launching on Monday, October 26, the Daily Mail's readers can discover how to put his research into practice – with the chance to feel happier and healthier within days, and potentially as a bonus even lose up to a stone in time for Christmas.
Based on Professor Spector’s research at ZOE, and including recipes from his new cookbook Good Mood Food, the series will guide you, step-by-step, through a new way of eating that could transform not just your waistline, but most importantly how you feel every day.
You'll discover the surprisingly simple foods that nourish the trillions of bacteria living in your gut, why these microbes may hold the key to better mood and brain health, and how to feed them.
We'll show you what to put in your shopping basket – and what to leave on the shelves – and how to build delicious, filling meals.
There will be exclusive recipes, from hearty breakfasts and satisfying dinners to indulgent desserts, along with expert advice on eating to support your mood and thinking as you get older.
Halfway through, Professor Spector will make a live appearance on dailymail.com to answer readers' questions and talk about his cookbook.
And as Christmas approaches he'll reveal how to enjoy your favourite festive foods without undoing all your hard work – and, crucially, how to make these changes stick for life.
Indeed, research by Professor Spector's gut health company ZOE found that 35 per cent of around 5,000 participants lost at least 5 per cent of their body weight in just three months.
Their approach to diet has become a global phenomenon, refined through years of research involving hundreds of thousands of people.
Although more personalised recommendations are available to ZOE subscribers, anyone can follow the basic principles, for free.
Becky overhauled her diet with the help of nutrition science company ZOE, co-founded by Professor Tim Spector, the scientist at the forefront of discoveries in diet and gut health
These include eating 30 different plants a week, by making simple tweaks such as sprinkling seeds, nuts or fresh herbs over a salad or soup, or adding chopped fruit or greens to a plate.
Professor Spector encourages dieters to swap meat, particularly processed meat such as sausages, bacon and salami, for plant-based proteins including beans, lentils and chickpeas, and to aim for at least 30g of fibre a day.
However, chicken, lean meat and especially oily fish can still be enjoyed as part of his approach.
Ultra-processed foods, or UPFs – industrially-produced foods lacking in nutrients and containing cosmetic additives designed to make food irresistible to eat – are discouraged.
Instead, meals should be based on whole foods, with a rainbow of different-coloured plants to maximise nutrients.
'Studies have found that people who eat healthy diets, full of fruit, vegetables and whole grains, significantly improve their mood,' Professor Spector says.
'On the other hand, people who eat the most UPFs such as crisps, biscuits, sausages, sugary soft drinks, chicken nuggets and sugary cereal, have the biggest risk of mental health problems and dementia.
'When people have moderate depression, giving them a gut-friendly diet can improve or reverse symptoms in a significant proportion of them.'
Despite this, processed foods such as baked beans, Weetabix and high-fibre or seeded bread are on the menu.
Fermented foods, including natural yogurt, sourdough bread, kefir, sauerkraut, kombucha and kimchi, also have a role to play, as do dark chocolate and peanut butter. Most of these feature in the cookbook.
'It's not about restriction or cutting out all processed foods,' he explains, 'it's about cutting back on the worst unhealthy ultra-processed foods and replacing them with real whole plants'.
Eating more whole foods increases fibre intake – nine in ten Britons fail to get the recommended 30g a day, which can help protect against bowel cancer, cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.
All ZOE studies to date have shown improvements in mood and energy within the first two weeks in the majority of people.
High-fibre foods also make you feel fuller for longer and can stimulate the release of GLP-1, the appetite-regulating hormone mimicked by weight-loss drugs.
Becky, now 52, is proof of how powerful these changes can be – with benefits she never expected.

articles.title_orig: Jensen Huang lobbied ‘very good friend’ Trump for more Nvidia sales to China while ‘caught in Beijing’s honeytrap’
articles.title_zh: Jensen Huang lobbied ‘very good friend’ Trump for more Nvidia sales to China while ‘caught in Beijing’s honeytrap’
articles.content_orig:
SAN FRANCISCO — Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang made himself President Trump’s “very good friend” and lobbied the administration to loosen restrictions on AI chip sales to China while he was allegedly ensnared in a Chinese honeytrap, a timeline of his reported relationship with Alice Huang shows.
The $150 billion AI boss appeared in loved-up snaps with accused communist spy Alice Huang last year — and then weeks later personally pitched Trump at the White House on relaxing export restrictions for the company’s chips.
Huang missed Trump’s second inauguration, but then more than made up for it with a $25 million donation to the president’s ballroom project.
The 63-year-old appeared at a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago in April 2025, where he pushed to lift chip restrictions that had just been imposed. There were at least three documented meetings between Trump and Huang where the administration responded with policy changes that made it easier for Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China.
China hawks have long pushed to restrict the most cutting edge chips from the communist regime in an attempt to blunt its technological advances and stymie its attempts to overtake the US on AI.
Huang, for his part, had lobbied and spoken out against restrictions since the Biden administration first imposed limits in 2022. Additionally, selling more chips to the world’s second largest economy could only help Nvidia’s bottom line.
But all the while, Huang — who has been married to college sweetheart Lori for more than 40 years — was meeting with 42-year-old Alice. In May 2025, they were spotted at dinner together during Taiwan’s top tech expo, where she looked at him adoringly and affectionately touched his arm as they sat with other tech honchos.
Alice Huang — a TV host, turned banker, turned executive at the Singapore-based AI computing company Megaspeed — met Jensen Huang (no relation) in early 2024, according to reports. Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars in chips from Nvidia for data centers in Southeast Asia and the Middle East.
Separately, the firm — backed by Chinese tech giant Alibaba — is under investigation for allegedly smuggling chips to China. The US government is probing reports that 50,000 chips sold to Megaspeed were seemingly missing following an audit.
Nvidia reportedly intervened in that probe, according to Bloomberg.
The Chinese government denies allegations of a honeypot spy scheme. Megaspeed also denies allegations of wrongdoing.
Trump himself has downplayed Huang’s admission of infidelity and Nvidia’s board said the company, which has no succession plan for replacing Huang, had full confidence in him, even as it announced it was investigating the claims.
On Monday, Trump said he called to check on Huang after he admitted cheating on his wife and apologized to his family.
“I did speak to him today just to see if he’s feeling all right,” Trump said at the White House. “He said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy. I asked him that question. Did you have any idea that she was a spy? He said I had no idea that she was a spy, and I really believe him.”
The president and the Nvidia “have become good friends,” a source close to them told The Post.
Huang has made himself an integral part of the US economy. Nvidia reached a historic $5.5 trillion in valuation in May 2026, beating out Apple at the time as the most valuable public company in the entire world. It is both the world’s most important chipmaker, and the locus around which the AI boom spins. It uses the profits from its sales to help fund AI companies building out data centers, spurring further demand for its products.
By some accounts the AI boom is expected to account for up to 4% of all US economic activity this year, and Nvidia’s revenues alone up to 1%.
Trump personally hailed Nvidia’s latest quarter record sales of $96.2 billion in September, up 106% from last year.
Huang notably traveled with the president during his trip to China last May, with Trump even going as far as to personally invite the Nvidia boss to ride with him on Air Force One.
When Huang couldn’t make it to Washington DC in time for departure, he took his private plane to Alaska to join the president during his refueling stop in Anchorage.
Dressed in his signature black leather jacket and carrying only a backpack, Jensen boarded the presidential plane alone, without an entourage, pausing to speak with Trump’s son Eric, who was also on the trip, as he boarded.
Huang and his wife were seated at the head table with the president and first lady Melania Trump at the September state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping . Trump was personally involved in selecting the guest list for that dinner, a source familiar with the planning told The Post.
Along with the gains for his company, Huang’s relationship with Trump reportedly came with some perks of power.
Huang called the president when his invitation to the April state dinner for King Charles arrived without a plus one, according to a source. The billionaire CEO wanted to bring his wife to the dinner.
When White House staff told him there were no plus ones, he called Trump and made a personal appeal, getting Lori Huang on the list and bumping a senior administration official off of it to make room for her, multiple administration sources told The Post.
Huang has two grown children with his wife, Spencer and Madison, who both work in their father’s company.
The family has a $38 million home in San Francisco , with Nvidia spending nearly $4 million in fiscal 2026 on services for Huang that included home security, protection during personal travel, consulting and drivers, according to its May proxy filing.
Huang has remained close to Trump, literally, traveling to the Middle East for Trump’s visit to Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates in May 2025, then to London to join the president at Windsor Castle for a state dinner with King Charles that September.
Trump, at a meeting with then-British Prime Minister Keir Starmer during that visit, saw the CEO in the audience and teasingly told him: “You’re taking over the world Jensen. I don’t know what you’re doing here. I hope you’re right.”
He also had a prime seat at Trump’s side at the September 29th meeting on AI policy , alongside other technology executives. And the president awarded him the National Medal of Science last month.
Huang and Trump remained close friends despite the warning signs about the Nvidia boss’ relationship with Alice, which one tech company flagged to the Commerce Department last summer.
“The White House has known how suspicious Ms. Huang, and her corporate network, is since last summer,” a source familiar with the case told The Post. “And Jensen has repeatedly lied about his relationship with Ms. Huang.”
Culper Research also published a report titled “NVIDIA (NVDA): The China Problem” in May 2026, which specifically warned about the concerning rumors about Nvidia’s chief executive and Alice.
Alice had been under investigation since the Biden administration and believed to have been recruited as an asset for China’s feared Ministry of State Security.
The Commerce Department first flagged Alice following her sudden rise to the top of Megaspeed in 2023.
The concerns were troubling enough that Secretary of State Marco Rubio pushed back on letting Huang attend the China state dinner with Trump, the source added.
Little is known about the alleged spy’s private life, but before entering the world of finance, Alice had worked as a reporter for CCTV, the national broadcaster of the Chinese state, and Hunan TV, a regional broadcaster in central China, according to her LinkedIn biography.
Local reports claimed Alice is married to former Shanghai Hexi chairman Kang Wei — a former business partner, whose firm was fined $2.7M and censured by the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Shares of The Trade Desk (NASDAQ:TTD) charged sharply higher on Monday, surging as much as 16.6%. As of 11:38 a.m. ET, the stock was still up 15.2%.
Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »
The catalyst that sent the digital advertising stock higher was anticipation regarding the company's upcoming financial report and the return of one of its founders.
Image source: Getty Images.
The Trade Desk announced last week that former chief technology officer (CTO) and co-founder Dave Pickles was returning after stepping down in 2023. Pickles will establish and lead the company's newly formed CTO council to "help shape the next generation of The Trade Desk platform." Pickles will focus "on aligning technology strategy, architectural direction, operational excellence, and key engineering investments--including agentic capabilities and advanced AI-powered advertising workflows."
Pickles is returning at a critical time for The Trade Desk. The company has floundered over the past year as slowing growth and increasing competition have weighed on its results. In the second quarter, The Trade Desk delivered revenue that grew just 3% year over year to $715 million, while its adjusted earnings per share (EPS) of $0.34 slumped 17%.
Perhaps even more concerning was the company's outlook, which called for revenue to decline 12% year over year to $650 million, while adjusted EBITDA of $160 million is expected to plunge 50%.
The return of Pickles has given investors hope that The Trade Desk can return to its former glory, but they may be getting ahead of themselves.
That said, the stock is trading for just 18 times earnings, near an all-time low set just last month. Given the pessimism built into the stock price, it wouldn't take much to send The Trade Desk higher -- as evidenced by its movement today.
We'll know more soon, as The Trade Desk is scheduled to report its Q3 results after the market close today.
Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.
While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.
Danny Vena, CPA has positions in The Trade Desk. The Motley Fool has positions in and recommends The Trade Desk. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy .

articles.title_zh: Brent at $90 a Barrel as Trump Plays Down Need For Further Iran Strikes
articles.content_orig:
Brent crude drops below $90 and markets climb after president downplays prospect of further strikes
Business live – latest updates
Oil prices have fallen to the lowest level since late August while stock markets climbed higher, as markets reacted with relief to Donald Trump saying that the war on Iran is “effectively over” .
Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, fell nearly 3% to $89.66, the lowest since 31 August, on Tuesday morning, after the US president downplayed the need for military action against Iran “at this point”. The fall came after a near 6% drop on Monday on signs that the conflict might be nearing an end.
Europe’s benchmark Stoxx 600 index gained 0.9% to 662.54, hovering near a record high, which it had hit in early August on hopes for a peace deal in the Middle East.
Airline stocks rose amid hopes that easing tensions could lead to lower fuel costs, with Lufthansa 1.8% ahead and Air France-KLM up 1.2%.
In London, the FTSE 100 index climbed 45 points, or 0.4%, to 10,828. The oil companies BP and Shell were the biggest losers, down 1.7% and 1.5% respectively.
During a White House press conference, Trump said Israel and Gulf allies in the region were well protected from Iran and an escalation was not needed.
“At this point, taking the military action doesn’t seem to be a very necessary thing – but we’re locked and loaded, ready to go for any reason,” he told reporters during a briefing at the White House.
Daniela Hathorn, a senior market analyst at the trading platform Capital.com, said: “Global markets are extending their recovery this morning after Wall Street recorded a strong session that was relatively broad-based, supported by a sharp decline in oil prices and renewed buying in technology stocks.”
However, the US Federal Reserve will want more evidence of slowing inflation, she said. The latest US inflation data for October will be released at 1.30pm GMT.
Hathorn added: “Ultimately, markets are benefiting from an improvement in the geopolitical outlook, but the underlying macroeconomic and corporate risks remain unresolved. Lower energy prices could help ease inflation expectations, but the Fed will need evidence of broader disinflation before reconsidering its policy stance.

“The key question is whether today’s inflation figures support the recovery or remind investors that resilient economic growth and persistent price pressures could keep borrowing costs elevated for longer. With technology valuations still sensitive to yields, another inflation surprise could quickly bring volatility back into focus.”
Drivers will hope the fall in wholesale oil prices continues to feed through to prices at the pump.
